## Introduction

For this assignment, I will be creating a HTML and JSON file with 3 books including multiple attributes. The following books will be manual entered into the file formats:

**Abstract Algebra**

- **Author**: David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote

- **ISBN:** 9780471433347

- **Copyright Year:** 2004

- **Publisher:** John Wiley & Sons, Incorporated

**Normal People**

- **Author:** Sally Rooney

- **ISBN:** 9781984822185

- **Copyright Year:** 2018

- **Publisher:** Crown / Hogarth

**Frankenstein**

- **Author:** Mary Shelley

- **ISBN:** NA

- **Copyright Year:** 1818

- **Publisher:** Lackington, Hughes, Harding, Mavor & Jones

## Approach

I first plan to create the HTML and JSON files in VS Code, and then load the data into R. I would expect that dataframes will be the same when loading from HTML and JSON. I have experience working with HTML and JSON files in R, but I have never created them manually. Creating the files will be the most challenging part of the assignment, but I am exciting to learn something new.

## Code

Before loading the HTML and JSON files into R, I manually created them in VS Code. Below is how I loaded them into R using the rvest abd jsonlite packages library:

```{r Libraries}
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(gt)
```

```{r Loading JSON}
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)

json_path <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EllieWilser/Data_607/refs/heads/main/Assignment_7/books.json"

book_table_json <- fromJSON(json_path)

book_table_json
```

```{r Loading HTML}

html_path <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EllieWilser/Data_607/refs/heads/main/Assignment_7/books.html"

html_content <- read_html(html_path)

table_list <- html_content %>% html_table()

book_table_html <- table_list[[1]]
```

Besides data types, the data frames after extracting are very similar. With authors, the main difference is that in json they were stored as a list instead of being comma separated.

```{r Cleaning Dataframes}
json_books_clean <- book_table_json |>
  unnest_wider(Author, names_sep="_") |>
  mutate(
    ISBN = as.character(ISBN),
  ) |>
  clean_names()

html_books_clean <- book_table_html |>
  mutate(ISBN = na_if(ISBN, "null")) |>
  separate_wider_delim(
    Authors,
    delim = ", ",
    names = c("Author_1", "Author_2"),
    too_few = "align_start"
  ) |> 
  clean_names()


```

```{r Display Results)}

json_books_clean |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title="JSON Data Extracted")

html_books_clean |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title="HTML Data Extracted")

```

From the table above, it can be seen that JSON and HTML loaded the exact same data. However, this was done after basic data cleaning and extracting.

## Conclusion

This assignment was great practice for me and helped me understand JSON and HTML formatting. I have little experience creating HTML and JSON files manual, so it was great practice. It was interesting to see how the file were loaded into R differently, practically how the multiple authors were loaded as lists instead of the dataframe. After cleaning, the tables were the exact same as I expected.

Future investigation can look at scrapping data from the web that uses these formats or working with APIs.
